Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency on the mid-sized prompts looks promising. We are starting to map out our Dedicated capacity ask for the MedEval pilot and want a ballpark footprint and cost delta for the following:

- Model target: MedEval LongContext-v2 (70B) — 65k token context required for ingestion/QA flows.
- Expected steady concurrency: 8 concurrent inference sessions (interactive flows), with occasional bursts to 24 concurrent. Average prompt length ~6k tokens, average generations ~1.2k tokens.
- QPS profile: ~3 requests/sec steady, peak ~10 req/sec.
- SLA needs: 95th latency target <1.2s for initial tokens, <250ms incremental per generated token.
- Security: must be in a dedicated pool (no shared tenancy).

Can you and the infra team give a sense of GPU count for a reserved GPU pool, and how that changes if we move to int8 / int4 quantization and if we enable persistent KV cache or prefer ephemeral per-session caches? Also any short notes on tradeoffs for canarying fallback variants for cost control would be helpful.

We're fast-tracking procurement — aim to have a proposal for internal review by Sept 24.

Best,

Hi all — I ran a quick footprint pass with the runtime team. Assumptions noted in the attached calc (footprint_calc.xlsx). High-level numbers below — these are conservative rounded estimates for capacity planning (network + overhead included).

Common inputs we used: model weights (70B) raw FP16 ~ 140 GB resident; KV cache multiplier assumes 1.25 bytes per token in KV (internal encoding) and the runtime keeps 2x active window margin for prefetched segments. We also assumed batching tuned to 8 concurrent sessions.

Scenario A — FP16 (no quant), ephemeral per-session KV:
- Weight memory per replica: ~140 GB (FP16) + host overhead ~12 GB = ~152 GB.
- KV cache per concurrent session (65k window + 1.2k average generation): ~66.2k tokens => ~83 MB/session (after runtime packing).
- With 8 steady concurrent sessions: KV resident ~664 MB. With bursts to 24: ~2 GB.
- Recommended GPU SKU: A100 80GB or 96GB-equivalent; each GPU can host 1 replica (weights reside on GPU).
- Required GPUs: steady 8 GPUs; to handle bursts without preempting, reserve 12 GPUs and allow burst autoscale to 24 (we can enable fast pre-warm).

Scenario B — int8 quant + persistent shared KV cache:
- Weight memory per replica: ~80 GB (int8 with optimized kernels) + host overhead ~8 GB => ~88 GB.
- Persistent KV cache shared across replicas: effective per-token storage reduced (cache dedupe and chunking) — we measured ~45 MB/session effective at this profile.
- With 8 steady sessions: KV ~360 MB. Bursts to 24: ~1.1 GB.
- Recommended GPU SKU: H100 or A100-80 with int8 kernels; each GPU can host 1 full replica; in some setups 2 replicas possible if memory headroom and quantization allow mixed allocation (but expect perf tradeoffs).
- Required GPUs: steady 6 GPUs (because weights smaller, can pack more aggressively) and reserved burst pool to 18 GPUs.

Scenario C — int4 aggressive quant + persistent KV + sharding:
- Weight memory per full replica: ~45 GB effective (int4 plus operator fusion) + host overhead ~6 GB = ~51 GB.
- With model sharding (2-way) we can split across 2 GPUs: each GPU holds ~26 GB of weights + KV overhead. Sharding adds inter-GPU comms latency (we budget ~8–12% latency hit).
- KV cache: similar to int8 shared cache (~40–50 MB/session).
- Recommended GPU SKU: H100 preferred for NVLink sharded config; two GPUs per replica in most cases.
- Required GPUs: steady capacity equivalent to 4 sharded replicas -> 8 GPUs (2 GPUs per replica), burst up to 16 GPUs for peak. This is the lowest GPU count but requires engineering for sharding, and expect slightly higher tail latency.

Tradeoffs / notes:
- Persistent shared KV reduces memory pressure significantly at the cost of cache-coherency logic; it's the largest wins for high context windows.
- int8 gives the best balance of latency and accuracy for most 70B instruction-tuned models; int4 is best for cost but needs validation for MedEval's QA fidelity.
- For the SLA, we recommend provisioning a dedicated warm pool (min warm GPUs = steady + 50% buffer) to avoid cold starts when users hit the burst.
- Canary strategy: deploy int8 as the primary variant, keep an FP16 fallback for high-SLA critical inference paths, and have an int4 cost tier for batch or low-priority workloads. Automatic fallback policy in the runtime can route requests based on current latency/cost targets.

I'll attach the calc and a quick chart — happy to refine once Sophie confirms burst duration and whether 65k is required for all flows.

-Marcus

Thanks Marcus — summarizing operational recommendation and next sales steps.

Operational recommendation (short):
1) Commit to an int8-first Dedicated pool in us-west with H100-class SKUs. Steady commit: 6 GPUs; burst policy to 18 for 3x traffic spikes. Warm pool: keep 2 spare hot GPUs for failover.
2) Enable persistent KV cache with a 48-hour eviction window for active documents (greatly reduces repeated fetch pressure).
3) Model rollout: start with int8 variant + A/B test a small percentage of requests to FP16 to measure QA regression. If FP16 accuracy delta > 1.5% on your evals we keep FP16 for critical routes.
4) For cost optimization: offer an int4-sharded batch tier for nightly batch re-processing of large documents. This tier cannot be used for interactive low-latency flows.

Sales / procurement asks for Biomed Solutions (Marissa):
- Would you prefer a monthly reserved commitment or a 12‑month reserved contract? We can show committed discounts for 12 months.
- We'll include two SKUs in the proposal: (A) int8-reserved baseline + burst credits; (B) FP16 guaranteed SLA option (higher price).

I'll prepare the pricing appendix and drop a proposal draft (dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf) into the Drive. Mina / Marissa: please let me know if you want the proposal to call out the fallback policies explicitly or keep them under "operational recommendations".

-Karthik
